def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 → Def2 𝓢 K → Def3 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    Def5 𝓑 F →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡘 F φ) →
    𝓢 ⊢ ⊥
a_raw: {"translation": "`Target` is the proposition asserting that for all types `Fm`, `S₀`, and `S`; all instances of `LogicalConnective Fm` and `LogicalNeutral Fm` (providing the formal connectives `🡒`, `⋏`, `⋎`, `∼` and constants `⊤`, `⊥` on `Fm`); all entailment relations `Entailment S₀ Fm` and `Entailment S Fm`; all proof systems `𝓑 : S₀` and `𝓢 : S` satisfying `Entailment.Cl 𝓑` and `Entailment.Cl 𝓢` (so each of `𝓑` and `𝓢` proves every classical propositional tautology in those connectives and is closed under modus ponens); and all functions `K : Fm → Fm` and `F : Fm → Fm`, if all seven of the following hypotheses hold: (1) `Def1 𝓑 K`: for every `φ : Fm`, if `𝓑 ⊢ φ` then `𝓑 ⊢ K φ`; (2) `𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢`: every sentence provable in `𝓑` is provable in `𝓢`; (3) `Def2 𝓢 K`: for all `φ, ψ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ)`; (4) `Def3 𝓢 K`: for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡒 φ`; (5) `Def4 𝓢 K`: for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 φ)`; (6) `Def5 𝓑 F`: there exists `ψ : Fm` such that `𝓑 ⊢ ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ)` (i.e., `𝓑 ⊢ (ψ 🡒 ∼(F ψ)) ⋏ (∼(F ψ) 🡒 ψ)`); and (7) for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡘 F φ` (i.e., `𝓢 ⊢ (K φ 🡒 F φ) ⋏ (F φ 🡒 K φ)`), then `𝓢 ⊢ ⊥` (`𝓢` proves the falsehood constant `⊥`). What is not required: `K` and `F` are arbitrary functions on `Fm` and need not be equal; neither `𝓑` nor `𝓢` is assumed consistent or given any structure beyond classical propositional logic and the stated hypotheses; closure under `φ ↦ K φ` (`Def1`) is assumed only for `𝓑` and `K` (not for `𝓢` and not for `F`); the schemata `Def2`, `Def3`, and `Def4` are assumed only for `𝓢` and `K` (not for `𝓑` and not for `F`); the sentence in `Def5` is assumed to exist only in `𝓑` and for `F` (not for `K`); the equivalence `K φ 🡘 F φ` for all `φ` is assumed to be provable only in `𝓢` (not in `𝓑`, and without assuming `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ)`); and the conclusion asserts `𝓢 ⊢ ⊥` rather than `𝓑 ⊢ ⊥`."}
translation: `Target` is the proposition asserting that for all types `Fm`, `S₀`, and `S`; all instances of `LogicalConnective Fm` and `LogicalNeutral Fm` (providing the formal connectives `🡒`, `⋏`, `⋎`, `∼` and constants `⊤`, `⊥` on `Fm`); all entailment relations `Entailment S₀ Fm` and `Entailment S Fm`; all proof systems `𝓑 : S₀` and `𝓢 : S` satisfying `Entailment.Cl 𝓑` and `Entailment.Cl 𝓢` (so each of `𝓑` and `𝓢` proves every classical propositional tautology in those connectives and is closed under modus ponens); and all functions `K : Fm → Fm` and `F : Fm → Fm`, if all seven of the following hypotheses hold: (1) `Def1 𝓑 K`: for every `φ : Fm`, if `𝓑 ⊢ φ` then `𝓑 ⊢ K φ`; (2) `𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢`: every sentence provable in `𝓑` is provable in `𝓢`; (3) `Def2 𝓢 K`: for all `φ, ψ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ)`; (4) `Def3 𝓢 K`: for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡒 φ`; (5) `Def4 𝓢 K`: for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 φ)`; (6) `Def5 𝓑 F`: there exists `ψ : Fm` such that `𝓑 ⊢ ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ)` (i.e., `𝓑 ⊢ (ψ 🡒 ∼(F ψ)) ⋏ (∼(F ψ) 🡒 ψ)`); and (7) for every `φ : Fm`, `𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡘 F φ` (i.e., `𝓢 ⊢ (K φ 🡒 F φ) ⋏ (F φ 🡒 K φ)`), then `𝓢 ⊢ ⊥` (`𝓢` proves the falsehood constant `⊥`). What is not required: `K` and `F` are arbitrary functions on `Fm` and need not be equal; neither `𝓑` nor `𝓢` is assumed consistent or given any structure beyond classical propositional logic and the stated hypotheses; closure under `φ ↦ K φ` (`Def1`) is assumed only for `𝓑` and `K` (not for `𝓢` and not for `F`); the schemata `Def2`, `Def3`, and `Def4` are assumed only for `𝓢` and `K` (not for `𝓑` and not for `F`); the sentence in `Def5` is assumed to exist only in `𝓑` and for `F` (not for `K`); the equivalence `K φ 🡘 F φ` for all `φ` is assumed to be provable only in `𝓢` (not in `𝓑`, and without assuming `𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ)`); and the conclusion asserts `𝓢 ⊢ ⊥` rather than `𝓑 ⊢ ⊥`.

divergences.description: The mechanistic hypothesis omits the outer knowledge operator K: Target assumes (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡘 F φ) rather than (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ)). Both Koellner's super strong mechanistic thesis ∃e K(K = F_e) and Alexander's schema K(Kφ ↔ ⌜φ⌝ ∈ W_m) (as well as the author's own claim) require that the equivalence between K and F be known; dropping the outer K turns the hypothesis into a sentence-by-sentence form of the weak mechanistic thesis (K = F_e). Because necessitation (Def1) is assumed only for 𝓑 and not for 𝓢, this omission also makes Target mathematically false (it is falsified by a two-world reflexive Kripke countermodel, e.g., Fm = Bool × Bool with 𝓑 as truth at both coordinates, 𝓢 as truth at the first coordinate, K(a, b) = (a ∧ b, b), F(a, b) = (a ∧ b, true), and ψ = (true, false)).

Target abstracts away arithmetic, Gödel numbering, Turing machines (F_e / W_m), the truth predicate of EA_T, and object-language quantifiers. Consequently, it cannot express Theorem 6's single object-language sentence ∃e K(K = F_e) in EA_T, instead working with arbitrary classical propositional systems 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢, an arbitrary function F : Fm → Fm with a postulated diagonal sentence (Def5 𝓑 F), and a meta-level schema over sentences φ for a fixed F (and without verifying that EA_T satisfies the abstract hypotheses or that ∃e K(K = F_e) reduces to the schema).

judgement.summary: Target diverges materially from Theorem 6 and Alexander's schema because its mechanistic hypothesis omits the outer K operator, asserting only 𝓢 ⊢ K φ 🡘 F φ (a weak mechanistic thesis schema) instead of 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ), which also renders the formalized proposition false. In addition, as an acknowledged abstraction, it does not model EA_T, arithmetic, Gödel numbering, Turing machines, or the object-language quantifiers in ∃e K(K = F_e).
